meta.title: nape-js — 2D Physics Engine for TypeScript & JavaScript
meta.description: nape-js is a fully typed 2D physics engine for TypeScript & JavaScript — rigid body dynamics, constraints, fluid buoyancy, raycasting, fracture, deterministic multiplayer, web worker. Tree-shakeable, zero dependencies, ~27 KB gzip. Free & open source (MIT).
home.hero.subtitle: Fully typed 2D physics engine for TypeScript & JavaScript — modern rewrite of Nape
home.hero.tagline: Rigid bodies • Circles, Polygons & Capsules • Constraints • Fluid simulation • Collision callbacks • Raycasting & spatial queries • Fracture • Soft body • Deterministic multiplayer • Serialization • Web Worker support — tree-shakeable, zero dependencies, ~27 KB gzip.

bench.heading: Benchmarks
bench.desc: Measured in your browser right now. Each test runs the physics step() in a tight loop and reports the median time per step.
features.heading: Why nape-js?
features.p1: nape-js is one of the few 2D physics engines for JavaScript and TypeScript that ships rigid body dynamics, joints (PivotJoint, DistanceJoint, WeldJoint, AngleJoint, MotorJoint, LineJoint, PulleyJoint, SpringJoint), fluid buoyancy, fracture, soft body, raycasting and convex sweeps, a built-in character controller, deterministic stepping for multiplayer rollback, binary serialization, replay recording, and an off-thread Web Worker bridge — all in a single tree-shakeable ESM bundle (~27 KB gzip), with full TypeScript types and zero DOM dependencies.
features.p2: Looking for an alternative to Box2D, Matter.js, Planck.js, or Rapier? Run the in-browser benchmark to compare them head-to-head, or jump into the interactive examples — physics demos and playable mini-games (platformer, MOBA, tower defense, slingshot, pinball, top-down shooter).
api.heading: API at a Glance
footer.credits: Based on the original Haxe engine by Luca Deltodesco • JS port scaffolded by Andrew Bradley • TypeScript rewrite & ongoing development by Istvan Krisztian Somoracz

examples.intro: 50+ interactive demos for the nape-js TypeScript physics engine. Tap or drag on the canvas to play with the simulation.
examples.mp.title: Multiplayer Physics
examples.mp.desc: Real-time server-authoritative simulation — move a character, push objects, see other players live.

demo.arena-defense.label: Arena Defense
demo.arena-defense.desc: Mash-up of top-down shooter + tower defense + portals + destructible bodies. Big 1800×1200 world with a camera that follows the player. Enemies enter from each side along a short L-shaped corridor and converge on the central base (HP 800, solid obstacle, auto-fires at the nearest enemy). Waves run on a fixed 12s cadence — a slow wave doesn't delay the next one, so pile-ups are part of the challenge. WASD move, Space dash (i-frames), auto-fire targets the nearest enemy. Step into a coloured portal to teleport. Every kill shatters the enemy via fractureBody (Voronoi shards) plus a short particle-emitter spark burst. Wave types: speed (dash-rushers), healer (green pulse-heals allies), and every 5th — a boss with shotgun, mines, summoned minions, and an AoE shockwave. Power-ups (40% drop): 2x/3x spread, EX explosive, RF rapid-fire, HP heal, SH shield, HM homing missiles.
demo.asteroid-field.label: Asteroid Field (Spatial Hash)
demo.asteroid-field.desc: 2000 asteroids drifting through space using the SPATIAL_HASH broadphase. Objects are spread out so most broadphase lookups skip narrowphase entirely — showcasing O(1) spatial hashing at scale. Click to spawn more.
demo.billiards.label: Billiards
demo.billiards.desc: Top-down billiards — zero-gravity table. Drag back from the cue ball to aim, release to break. High-restitution balls clack and roll with friction toward six sensor pockets; sinking the cue is a scratch. Input locks until the table settles.
demo.body-from-graphic.label: Body From Graphic
demo.body-from-graphic.desc: Uses MarchingSquares to extract physics bodies from the cog bitmap. Three sizes, each processed independently. Drag any cog with the mouse.
demo.brickline.label: Brickline
demo.brickline.desc: Stack-as-high-as-you-can arcade demo. A KINEMATIC brick slides above the tower; click / Space converts it to DYNAMIC so it drops onto the stack. Stability comes purely from rigid-body contact and high Material.staticFriction. Drop a brick too far off-centre and the tower tips. Camera follows the stack top up. Showcases kinematic → dynamic conversion, friction-only stacking, and centre-of-mass tipping.
demo.capsule.label: Capsule Shapes
demo.capsule.desc: Native capsule-shaped bodies (two semicircular end-caps + rectangle middle) collide and stack. Click to spawn more capsules.
demo.car-sideview.label: 2D Car — Side View
demo.car-sideview.desc: A car with SpringJoint suspension on wavy terrain. Use ← → arrow keys or tap left/right to drive.
demo.car-topdown.label: 2D Car — Top Down
demo.car-topdown.desc: Top-down racing car with arcade physics on a winding rally track. Use ↑ ↓ ← → arrow keys (or WASD), Space for handbrake/drift, Shift to brake. On touch: tap front/back to throttle/brake, left/right to steer.
demo.chain.label: Pendulum Chain
demo.chain.desc: A pendulum chain with a heavy bob. Drag any link to grab and pull it.
demo.character-controller.label: Character Controller
demo.character-controller.desc: WASD/Arrow keys to move, Space to jump. Features: slopes, one-way platforms, moving platforms, wall-slide, wall-jump, ice, coyote time. Uses the built-in CharacterController class with dynamic body physics.
demo.cloth.label: Cloth Simulation
demo.cloth.desc: A grid of particles connected by springs, simulating cloth with a logo texture. Drag the cloth with the mouse. A circle obstacle drifts across.
demo.constraints.label: Constraints Showcase
demo.constraints.desc: All 8 built-in constraint types in a 3×3 grid. Drag any body to feel how each constraint reacts.
demo.contraption-garage.label: Contraption Garage
demo.contraption-garage.desc: Fantastic-Contraption-style vehicle builder. In the build zone, click to place powered wheels (drive right / drive left) and frame nodes, and drag part-to-part to connect them with springy rods. Hit Test: rods become soft DistanceJoints, each wheel drives via a MotorJoint against its frame, and the camera follows your machine down a three-screen course — pit, whoop bumps, a gap to bridge, a stair climb and a cliff chute. Reaching the flag yourself wins nothing: a pink cargo ball waits on the high plateau, and IT has to get to the flag. Driven rims kick the ball away with backspin, so a bare car just tramples it — try a reverse-spinning wheel as an intake roller, and bring enough traction to push the cargo up the final ramp. Rods show live strain and snap when overloaded, mid-test you can grab parts with a springy pivot hand, and parts overlap freely thanks to InteractionFilter groups. Space toggles test, 1–4 pick tools, R resets.
demo.convex-cast.label: Convex Cast
demo.convex-cast.desc: A spinning blade sweeps obstacles using space.convexCast() and space.convexMultiCast(). The red marker is the first hit in the next frame; yellow dots are all hits within the next 0.35 s. Click to spawn dynamic bodies into the sweep zone.
demo.conveyor-belts.label: Conveyor Belts
demo.conveyor-belts.desc: Objects travel along conveyor belts using kinematic surface velocity.
demo.crash-test-hero.label: Crash Test Hero
demo.crash-test-hero.desc: Turbo-Dismount-style crash scoring. Pose the ragdoll dummy on its cart by dragging any body part, then hold Space (or the LAUNCH button) to charge the ping-ponging power meter and release to launch it down the ramp, over the pit, down the staircase and into the trampoline, the spinning paddle wheel and the crate wall. Damage IS the score — every hard contact pays out points from measured totalContactsImpulse (head hits ×3), and the seatbelt, neck, shoulders and hips are real breakable constraints (maxForce + breakUnderForce) that snap for bonus points via a ConstraintListener(BREAK). Big hits freeze time and shake the camera. On the way down time nearly freezes — press Space again to eject the dummy at the fast-sweeping aim arrow's angle, FlatOut-style, into the obstacle gauntlet: bowling pins, wrecking balls, a field of spinning rotors only a good arc can reach, a seesaw and the crate wall. After ejecting, Space panic-flails (3 charges). R restarts.
demo.destructible-arena.label: Destructible Arena
demo.destructible-arena.desc: Side-view shooter built from buildTilemapBody + CharacterController + two ParticleEmitters + fractureBody. The arena is 3× canvas-wide; the camera follows the player and shakes on every kill. WASD/Arrows move, Space jumps. Hold into a wall mid-air to wall-slide, and press Space to wall-jump off it. Jump up through the purple one-way platforms; the cyan platform glides back and forth as a kinematic body. Hold mouse to fire toward the cursor.
demo.destructible-terrain.label: Destructible Terrain
demo.destructible-terrain.desc: Procedural terrain built with MarchingSquares. Click to blast holes. Dynamic shapes spawn and interact with the evolving terrain.
demo.deterministic.label: Deterministic Mode
demo.deterministic.desc: Two identical simulations run side by side with space.deterministic = true. Every position matches bit-for-bit. Click to drop shapes into both.
demo.dirtline.label: Dirtline
demo.dirtline.desc: Hill-climb trials bike with an articulated ragdoll rider welded to the seat, on a long course with several big jumps. → / D throttle, ← / A reverse, ↑ / W lean back (pop the front), ↓ / S lean forward (nose-down). The moving wheels fling physics-based gravel that skitters on the track. Flip the bike or smack the ground hard and the rider breaks away and ragdolls off. R or click to respawn. Showcases MotorJoint wheels on SpringJoint suspension, a ragdoll attached to a moving vehicle, a break-away WeldJoint, and a terrain-only ParticleEmitter.
demo.dominos.label: Dominos
demo.dominos.desc: A chain of thin dominos that topple one after another. Click to drop a ball.
demo.drop-image-body.label: Drop Image → Body
demo.drop-image-body.desc: Drag any image file onto the canvas — MarchingSquares extracts the physics contour instantly and spawns a dynamic body. Drag bodies with the mouse.
demo.exploding-50.label: Exploding 50
demo.exploding-50.desc: 50 GitHub stars! 🎉 The number 50, built from hundreds of rigid blocks, charges up then detonates with a radial impulse — hard-hit blocks shatter into four — before re-assembling. Click to blow it up early.
demo.explosion.label: Impulse Blast
demo.explosion.desc: Click anywhere to create an impulse blast that pushes nearby bodies away.
demo.falling.label: Falling Shapes
demo.falling.desc: Random boxes and circles fall into a container. Click to spawn more shapes at the cursor.
demo.filtering-interactions.label: Filtering Interactions
demo.filtering-interactions.desc: Demonstrates all three interaction types via InteractionFilter bitmasks: collision (boxes bounce off each other), sensor (circles detect overlaps without physics response), and fluid (pentagons experience buoyancy). Click to spawn more shapes.
demo.floppy-fists.label: Floppy Fists
demo.floppy-fists.desc: Two ragdoll brawlers fight in a tiny ring — knock the opponent out (HP ≤ 0) or off the platform. Limbs are driven by mutating AngleJoint targets each frame (motor-like control without MotorJoint); InteractionListener tallies damage from contact impulse. P1: A/D move, W jump, F jab, G kick, H heavy. P2: arrows + J/K/L, or AI. Press T to toggle AI/2P, R to restart, I for help.
demo.fluid-buoyancy.label: Fluid & Buoyancy
demo.fluid-buoyancy.desc: Objects with different densities interact with a fluid pool — light ones float, heavy ones sink. A small boat bobs on the waves. Click to drop objects.
demo.fracture.label: Voronoi Fracture
demo.fracture.desc: Click on objects to shatter them with Voronoi fracture. Fragments can be re-fractured! Scroll to change blast radius.
demo.funnel.label: Funnel
demo.funnel.desc: Shapes pour through a funnel into a container. Click to add more shapes.
demo.gravity.label: Orbital Gravity
demo.gravity.desc: Mario Galaxy-style gravity: bodies are pulled toward a central planet via RadialGravityField. Click to spawn orbiting bodies.
demo.minigolf.label: Minigolf
demo.minigolf.desc: Top-down minigolf — zero-gravity table, drag from the ball to aim, release to putt. Slope zones (sensor-driven force fields) curve your shot; the hole is a TriggerZone sensor. Press R to retry the hole.
demo.moba-lite.label: MOBA-lite
demo.moba-lite.desc: Rough MOBA sketch — three lanes through a triangle-island maze, creep waves, 12 towers and two Ancients. Move with WASD (or bottom-left virtual stick); auto-attack fires at the nearest enemy in range. Q drops a 2s mine that bursts into 10 radial bullets, E is a dash with short i-frames. Earn gold + XP by killing creeps/towers; level up to 10. Shop buttons at the top-left buy +3 DMG or heal 50. Destroy the red Ancient ★ to win; lose if the blue Ancient falls. Camera follows the player across the 1800×1000 world.
demo.newtons-cradle.label: Newton's Cradle
demo.newtons-cradle.desc: Classic Newton's Cradle demonstrating conservation of momentum and energy.
demo.one-way-platforms.label: One-Way Platforms
demo.one-way-platforms.desc: Bodies pass through platforms from below but rest on them from above. Click & drag a body to pull it through a platform — release to watch it land. Click empty space to spawn a new shape. The bottom conveyor belt pushes shapes sideways.
demo.performance-profiler.label: Performance Profiler
demo.performance-profiler.desc: Real-time physics profiler overlay — shows per-phase step timing, body/contact/constraint counters, and a rolling time graph. Click to spawn shapes and watch metrics change.
demo.pinball.label: Pinball
demo.pinball.desc: Pinball with asymmetric bumpers, slingshots, pegs, a launch lane, and an oscillating blocker. Left/Right arrows or A/D to flip. Click left/right half to flip on mobile. Click upper area to spawn balls.
demo.planet-platformer.label: Planet Platformer
demo.planet-platformer.desc: Walk around eight planetoids — each with its own RadialGravityField, including a giant Goliath in the east. Gravity points toward the nearest planet, the CharacterController.down direction is updated each frame, so jumping, slope-walking and ground detection all work in any orientation. The camera follows the player across the world. Collect coins and reach the ★ star on top of Goliath. WASD/Arrows + Space.
demo.plinko.label: Plinko
demo.plinko.desc: 1000 balls cascade through a dense staggered peg field, settle into slots, and recycle back to the top.
demo.popcorn.label: Popcorn
demo.popcorn.desc: 200 kernels rest in a hot bowl. While they sit on the heat, each one suddenly grows (its Circle.radius is mutated at runtime), gets a small upward kick and spin, then fluffs into a popcorn cloud. Kernels pop while they're inside the bowl or after they tumble out into the flame below it — anywhere else they just fall harmlessly back down. The kinematic bowl jiggles on every pop and the camera shakes with it.
demo.portals.label: Portals
demo.portals.desc: Portal physics with UserConstraint and callbacks. Drag shapes into portals — they emerge from the linked partner.
demo.pulley-crane.label: Pulley Lift
demo.pulley-crane.desc: A rigid rope over two pulley wheels couples a cabin (left) and a counterweight (right). PulleyJoint enforces a fixed total rope length, so adding cargo to one side sinks it and lifts the other. Click the left half to drop a ball into the cabin, the right half to drop a weight onto the counterweight.
demo.pyramid.label: Pyramid Stress Test
demo.pyramid.desc: A classic box-stacking pyramid. Click to drop a heavy ball onto it.
demo.raft-rapids.label: Raft Rapids
demo.raft-rapids.desc: Build-a-raft passenger run on real fluid buoyancy. In the loading bay, click to place floating barrels, deck nodes and wind-catching sails, and drag part-to-part to connect them with springy rods. Hit Launch: the raft splashes in, the crane lowers a ragdoll passenger who is denser than water — overboard he goes under and the run is lost — and the current carries everything down a four-screen river: a staircase of three waterfalls, each taller than the last, with boulder slaloms and accelerating headraces between them, to the delivery dock. The passenger holds on with a breakable joint: slalom bumps he rides out, a big drop tears his grip and he tumbles — and if the current washes the raft back under him, he grabs hold again. Rods are soft DistanceJoints with live strain that snap on hard rock hits, and sails pull toward a gusty tailwind while they stay dry. Once you launch, the run is hands-off: the raft you designed either makes it or it doesn't. Space launches, 1–4 pick tools, R resets.
demo.ragdoll.label: Ragdoll
demo.ragdoll.desc: Ragdoll figures built from PivotJoint and AngleJoint constraints. Click to spawn a new ragdoll at the cursor.
demo.ragdoll-royale.label: Ragdoll Royale
demo.ragdoll-royale.desc: Battle-royale spectator sport with 50 numbered ragdolls standing to attention across five decks. The world holds its breath until you make your one decision (click a dummy to bet on it, Space picks at random) — then a seeded hazard schedule eats the arena: telegraphed geyser blasts, ball cannons that ride up and down the walls, rockfall from telegraphed ceiling hatches, platforms yanked from under everyone, kinematic rotors that reverse at random while riding their shafts, and a floor that crumbles in random order into the void. Damage is measured, not scripted — hard contacts bruise via totalContactsImpulse, necks/shoulders/hips are breakable constraints that tear off under violent yanks, and 0% is a KO. Last dummy in play wins; the banner grades your bet by placement. Per-rig InteractionGroup keeps 500 ragdoll parts colliding with each other but never with themselves. Every round reseeds — R restarts.
demo.cargo-crane.label: Cargo Crane Captain
demo.cargo-crane.desc: Load ten crates onto a barge that actually floats — a fluid-enabled water body, not a static platform. A real PulleyJoint hauls a live counterweight up its guide as the winch pays out; drive the trolley, then SPACE to grab and release. Every crate you set down shifts the barge's buoyancy, so a lopsided load makes it list — and enough list capsizes it. Miss the deck and the crate sinks; slam one hard enough and it shatters. ←/→ trolley, ↑/↓ winch, R restart.
demo.replay-recorder.label: Deterministic Replay
demo.replay-recorder.desc: Demonstrates Recorder + Player from @newkrok/nape-js/replay. Press Record, click to throw balls, Stop, then Replay — the recorded clicks reproduce identical physics.
demo.rollercoaster.label: Rollercoaster
demo.rollercoaster.desc: A 6-car train with sprung suspension rolls along a long hilly track. Each car carries upright capsule passengers pinned by the feet — they sway forward and back through every drop and crest. Pure gravity, no motors.
demo.rope-bridge.label: Rope Bridge
demo.rope-bridge.desc: A bridge made of planks connected by PivotJoints. Click to drop heavy objects onto it.
demo.save-load-rewind.label: Save / Load / Rewind
demo.save-load-rewind.desc: Demonstrates spaceToBinary / spaceFromBinary. Click to detonate a blast. Drag the timeline to scrub through the last 3 seconds. Save 1-5 to capture state, Load to restore, Branch to fork a new timeline from the scrubbed point.
demo.seesaw.label: Seesaw
demo.seesaw.desc: A balanced seesaw that tilts when objects land on it. Click to drop heavy balls.
demo.sky-hook.label: Sky Hook
demo.sky-hook.desc: Helicopter medevac with slung ragdolls — three patients stranded across a canyon, the hospital pad in the middle. Fly with arrows/WASD (hold the pointer to steer on touch), hover the chain-link rope's hook by a patient and press Space to winch him into the harness — then carry him swinging under the chopper past towers, a bridge underpass, blocks hanging from the sky, patrolling platforms, wrecking balls and spinning X / I / cross rotors back to the hospital. Necks, shoulders and hips are real breakable constraints (maxForce + breakUnderForce) — slam a patient and limbs tear off; yank hard enough and the harness snaps. Every hard contact chips the chopper's hull via measured totalContactsImpulse — at zero it drops out of the sky. Space releases, R restarts.
demo.slingshot.label: Slingshot Siege
demo.slingshot.desc: Drag from the slingshot to aim, release to fire! Balls shatter the castle on impact. Click slingshot to reload.
demo.soft-body.label: Soft Body
demo.soft-body.desc: Pneumatic soft bodies: a trapezoidal shell with stiff outer skin, elastic inner skin, and gas-pressure volume conservation.
demo.spring-joint.label: Spring / Damper Joint
demo.spring-joint.desc: SpringJoint demo — spring chain and soft-body blob. Drag any body to interact.
demo.stacking.label: Stacking
demo.stacking.desc: Towers of various shapes testing stacking stability. Click to drop a heavy box.
demo.standoff.label: Standoff
demo.standoff.desc: A top-down stand-still-to-shoot roguelite. Your hero auto-fires at the nearest foe only while standing still — the instant you move, the weapon goes cold, so each fight is stop-shoot-dodge. Clear every enemy in a room and draft one of three permanent perks that stack for the whole run: extra arrow directions (front, side, rear, diagonal), routing (piercing, wall ricochet, enemy-to-enemy ricochet), payload (explosive shot, bolt chain lightning, freeze, poison), companions (spirit orbs), and stats (crit, damage, speed, bloodthirst, quickdraw). Cleared rooms open a random-wall exit door; walking into it fades to the next arena. Melee rush with charges, ranged kite and snipe, dashers blink in, and every 5th room is a boss with shotguns and bullet rings. Deeper rooms add active hazards: telegraphed spike traps, lava pools, and spinning sawblades (kinematic bars that sweep the arena and block shots). Fallen enemies sometimes drop a healing heart — walk over it while wounded to patch up. Move with WASD / arrows or the bottom-left virtual stick. Camera shake on every kill, hit, trap, and boss slam.
demo.sticky-builder.label: Sticky Builder
demo.sticky-builder.desc: Physics construction game. Drag a spare blob near the truss and release to weld it in with springy DistanceJoint struts (soft constraints — stiff=false). Bridge the wide chasm — a mid-span rock pillar helps — and reach the beacon above the far platform before the spare blobs run out; on connect the survivors march home along the struts. Struts show live strain and snap when overstretched — yank a welded node (springy PivotJoint hand) to tear the truss apart and reclaim its blob. The seed's feet are pinned with PivotJoint anchors, and blobs never collide with each other thanks to InteractionFilter groups.
demo.strandbeast.label: Strand Beast
demo.strandbeast.desc: A Theo Jansen-style walking mechanism with 6 legs (3 phase-offset pairs) driven by a MotorJoint crank. Reverses direction at the walls. Click to drop a ball.
demo.sub-stepping.label: Sub-Stepping Solver
demo.sub-stepping.desc: A 14-row pyramid under low solver iterations. Left: subSteps=1 — jitters endlessly (orange). Right: subSteps=4 — settles to sleep (green). Click to drop more boxes.
demo.three-body.label: Three-Body Problem
demo.three-body.desc: Three masses, mutual gravity, no closed-form solution. Switch between the famous figure-8 orbit, the rotating Lagrange triangle, a sun + planets system, or pure chaos. Click a body to perturb it.
demo.tilemap.label: Tilemap (Greedy Meshing)
demo.tilemap.desc: A 108×40 procedurally-generated platformer level converted to physics with buildTilemapBody. Greedy meshing reduces hundreds of solid tiles into a handful of rectangles. Procedurally-textured dirt + grass tiles, camera follows the player. Click a tile to toggle solid/empty (rebuilds the body). WASD/Arrows + Space to play. O toggles greedy-rect overlay.
demo.tiltrun.label: Tilt-Run Marble Maze
demo.tiltrun.desc: Top-down tilt-maze. Move the pointer away from the maze centre to tilt the world — gravity points toward the cursor. Roll the marble through three labyrinths to the green goal while collecting gold coins and avoiding red pits. Showcases dynamic space.gravity, sensor-driven game state, and the buildTilemapBody helper.
demo.tinywheels-cup.label: Tinywheels Cup
demo.tinywheels-cup.desc: Top-down kart-racer — you (blue) vs. three waypoint-driven AI opponents on a closed three-lap track. Mario-Kart-style item boxes: pick up a ?-pad to roll a random item into your slot, then E to fire it. Mushroom = speed burst, Bolt = slow all rivals, Banana = drop trap behind, Shell = forward projectile. Watch for rotating bars and bouncy balls — they'll knock you off-line. Controls: ↑ ↓ ← → (or WASD), Space brake, Shift drift, E use item. First to three laps wins.
demo.top-down-shooter.label: Top-down Shooter
demo.top-down-shooter.desc: Top-down survival shooter — enemies pour in from 4 spawn points, every 5th wave closes with a boss that rushes, drops mines and fires shotguns. Melee chase you with burst rushes, ranged keep distance and snipe. Movement: WASD or bottom-left virtual stick (mobile). Auto-fire targets the nearest enemy; walls block bullets. 40% enemy drop chance for 10s power-ups: 2x / 3x spread, KB knockback blast, EX explosive AOE bullets, RF rapid fire, HP instant heal.
demo.tower-defense.label: Tower Defense
demo.tower-defense.desc: Build archer (single-target) and bomb (AOE + knockback) towers to defend the base. Enemies are physics bodies — bombs scatter them against walls, and they fight their way back on track. Click empty spot to build, click tower to upgrade. Enemy HP scales with wave; every 3rd wave brings fast runners, every 5th wave is a horde that pours in 5-at-a-time.
demo.tracked-vehicle.label: Tracked Vehicle
demo.tracked-vehicle.desc: Tank-style tracked vehicle with a cannon. Drive with ← → (or A/D), aim with ↑ ↓ (or W/S), fire with Space. Shells blast destructible terrain.
demo.trebuchet.label: Trebuchet
demo.trebuchet.desc: A counterweight trebuchet that launches projectiles. Click to reload and fire.
demo.trigger-zones.label: Trigger Zones
demo.trigger-zones.desc: Bodies fall through colored trigger zones (circle, box, polygon). Counters show enter/exit events and current occupancy — powered by the high-level TriggerZone API.
demo.volcano.label: Volcano
demo.volcano.desc: Physics-aware particles. A vent fires lava drops upward in a 40-degree cone; a RadialGravityField pulls every drop back to the planet, where it collides with the rocky debris on the surface. Click to detonate a 60-particle burst at the cursor — sparks bounce off the world like any other dynamic body. ~600 live particles at 60 FPS.
demo.web-worker.label: Web Worker Physics
demo.web-worker.desc: Physics simulation runs off the main thread in a Web Worker. 300 bodies at 60 Hz — main thread only renders. Click to spawn shapes + impulse blast.
demo.wrecking-ball.label: Wrecking Ball
demo.wrecking-ball.desc: A heavy ball on a chain smashes into a tower of boxes. Click to reset the swing.
demo.wyrm.label: Wyrm
demo.wyrm.desc: A one-button endless runner. Hold Space (or tap & hold) to thrust upward, release to fall. The tunnel of static Polygon strips is generated ahead of the player and culled behind. Grab ★ stars for points — sensor-only bodies that burst into dynamic shards on pickup (the shards collide with the walls but pass through you via collision filters). Showcases per-frame body.force, camera follow + shake on crash, parallax background, procedural spawn/cleanup, and SENSOR-mode InteractionListeners.
